summary: Iteration 15 — Gender filter on groups: FULLY VERIFIED end-to-end. BACKEND (20/20 pytest in /app/backend/tests/test_gender_filter.py, 100%): CREATE — user with gender=null cannot create male/female group (400 'Imposta il tuo sesso nel profilo...'); male user cannot create 'solo donne' group (400 'Non puoi creare un gruppo "solo donne"...'); female user cannot create 'solo uomini' group (400 'Non puoi creare un gruppo "solo uomini"...'); female creating female group → 200 and doc persisted with gender_filter='female' (verified via direct DB read + GET /api/groups/{id}); male creating male group → 200; any-gender + gender_filter='any' → 200; omitted gender_filter field → 200 with default 'any'; user with gender=null CAN create 'any' group. JOIN — user with gender=null joining male group → 400 with 'sesso ... profilo'; female user joining male group → 403 'Questo gruppo è riservato solo agli uomini.'; male user joining female group → 403 'Questo gruppo è riservato solo alle donne.'; same-gender user joins → 200 and is added to participants. LEGACY — group inserted directly without gender_filter field → GET /api/groups and GET /api/groups/{id} both return gender_filter:'any'; a gender=null user can freely join a legacy group. AGE+GENDER interaction — female-only 18+ group correctly 403s a male-25 (gender check) AND a female-15 (age-bucket check); both dimensions enforced. REGRESSION — /api/auth/session google-auth suite (16/16) still passes; GET /api/groups always includes 'gender_filter' key. FRONTEND (Expo web at http://localhost:3000, viewport 390x844) — seeded a male user + token via MongoDB, bootstrapped via localStorage.groupup_session_token; ALL 5 checks pass: (1) 'Solo donne' badge shown on the female-only card in the feed, (2) Crea tab renders 3 chips with testIDs gender-filter-any/male/female, (3) for male user the gender-filter-female chip has computed opacity=0.35 and clicking it does NOT change state, (4) clicking gender-filter-male activates the chip (background rgb(255,230,0) vs rgb(255,255,255) for inactive), (5) /group/{id} detail page renders 'Solo donne' info row with the female icon. NO console errors. No regressions detected.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:106 GroupCreate.gender_filter uses Literal['male','female','any'] with default 'any' — correct default, correct type, backward-compat with clients that omit the field (verified by test_omitted_gender_filter_defaults_to_any).

server.py:967-972 _group_doc_to_model.setdefault('gender_filter','any') — clean backward-compat shim; ensures every legacy doc surfaces as 'any' at the API boundary. Verified by TestLegacyGroupsNoGenderFilter.

server.py:992-1006 POST /api/groups gender policy — correctly refuses (a) gender_filter in ('male','female') without user.gender (400) and (b) mismatched gender (400 with the exact Italian strings). Runs BEFORE age validation so it doesn't leak past-date/age errors when the caller is genuinely blocked by gender.

server.py:1184-1199 join_group gender policy — correctly evaluates AFTER the age-bucket check; 400 for missing profile gender, 403 for a genuine mismatch with distinct male/female wording. Legacy groups short-circuit via `g_gender or 'any'`.

frontend/app/(tabs)/create.tsx:469-470 the disabled chip is computed from user.gender rather than from the chip key alone — this means a user with gender=null can still tap either restricted chip (state changes locally) and hit the client-side validation on submit (lines 162-176). Matches spec 'submitting must show the client-side error'. Verified live.
frontend/app/(tabs)/create.tsx:197 payload includes gender_filter — no risk of the field being dropped on the wire.
frontend/app/(tabs)/index.tsx:161-171 card badge uses conditional icon (👨/👩) + label — visually distinct from the age/participants badges, correctly hidden for gender_filter==='any'.
frontend/app/group/[id].tsx:257-268 info row uses the ionicon name 'male'/'female' — matches the badge on the feed for consistency; row is skipped when gender_filter==='any'.

frontend/src/lib/api.ts ApiGroup type — gender_filter is optional (?), so pre-migration types still compile; consumers must handle undefined ⇒ 'any' — index.tsx and [id].tsx both check strict equality on 'male'/'female', so undefined falls through correctly.
